baseline_note: baseline_min_area_* is MathWorld's row transported to the unit-radius disk (alpha = pi * H). It is retained only so the repo's standalone verify_disk_configs.py has a numeric field to compare; it is NOT the authority. See circle_baseline.py: MathWorld's n=11 row is erroneous.
claim: NOT a new result. This value lies inside the published bracket for the unit-radius circle, so it is an independent REDISCOVERY of the known configuration, reached from random starts with no prior knowledge of it. Retained as an exactly certified witness only.
known_result_attribution: David Cantrell, August 2006 (Friedman's circle page: '.113+', horizontally symmetric)
mathworld_erratum: MathWorld's n=11 row (0.03494193340280051 unit-area = 0.109773530502 unit-radius) is below Friedman/Cantrell's .113+ unit-radius value. MathWorld is in error; Friedman is primary.
method: multistart simulated annealing (C, pthreads, boundary-count cycled over 3..n across restarts) -> sequential-LP polish (scipy/HiGHS) -> snap to a 1/scale integer grid -> exact rational minimum triangle area with an exact closed-unit-disk containment check
